context.objective: Enable employees to submit expenses in the existing employee portal, route required approvals, and support Finance reimbursement handling.
context.current_task: Review the ExpPay requirements analysis and resolve feature-specific decision debt before implementation and complete QA test design.
in_scope: Employee expense submission in the existing employee portal
Approval routing by payment method and amount
out_of_scope: Selection of a specific corporate card vendor
Unstated user-interface, storage, accounting, payroll, or integration designs
actors: Employee — submits expenses and may revise and resubmit rejected expenses (SUPPORTED)
Direct manager — approves expenses under the stated matrix (SUPPORTED)
Next-level manager — provides additional approval for expenses of $101 or more (SUPPORTED)
Finance — handles reimbursement and uses QuickBooks expense types for tax reporting (SUPPORTED)
systems: Unspecified corporate card vendor (SUPPORTED; requirements must remain vendor-neutral)
authoritative_sources: Stakeholder opening statement and supplied answers in the 2026-09-21 conformance exercise
confirmed_business_rules: Employees submit expenses in the existing employee portal; managers approve them and Finance handles reimbursement.
Corporate card expenses of $25 or less are automatically approved.
Corporate card expenses from $26 through $100 require the employee's direct manager.
Corporate card expenses of $101 or more require the direct manager and next-level manager.
Expenses not paid with a corporate card always require the direct manager and, at $101 or more, also require the next-level manager.
Expense categories mirror QuickBooks expense types used by Finance for tax reporting; no additional category-specific limits have been defined.
Receipts are required for expenses of $26 or more.
Corporate card expenses are paid directly to the card vendor, and requirements must not be tied to a specific card vendor.
Approved out-of-pocket reimbursements go through the employee's next scheduled payroll deposit.
An employee can revise and resubmit a rejected expense.
Expenses must be submitted within 60 days.
derived_facts: Expense amount and corporate-card status must be available to evaluate approval routing.
Receipt evidence must be available when the receipt rule is evaluated.
Dates sufficient to evaluate the 60-day interval must be available.
For presentation of the supplied non-card routing rules, a non-card expense of $100 or less requires only direct-manager approval.
constraints: Requirements must remain independent of a specific corporate card vendor.
Policy wording must not be converted into unsupported blocking, rejection, escalation, or other enforcement behavior.
terminology: Corporate card expense — an expense paid with a corporate card.
Out-of-pocket expense — used in the supplied evidence for an employee reimbursement delivered through payroll.
Next-level manager — the manager approval level in addition to the employee's direct manager for expenses of $101 or more.

open_questions.question: From which event is the 60-day submission interval measured, how is it counted, and what happens when it is exceeded?
What are the authoritative QuickBooks expense types, and how must ExpPay obtain, refresh, and map them?
How are approved out-of-pocket expenses handed to payroll, including cutoff, exception, correction, and failed-payment handling?
How is payment to a corporate card vendor initiated and reconciled while remaining vendor-neutral?
Are direct-manager and next-level-manager approvals sequential or parallel, and what happens if either rejects?
What behavior applies when a required receipt is absent?
What currency and amount-normalization rules govern the dollar thresholds, including fractional amounts, credits, and zero amounts?
What rejection reasons, comments, editable fields, and history are needed on revision and resubmission?

decision_debt.decision: Define the 60-day interval and late-submission consequence.
Define the authoritative category set and QuickBooks synchronization or mapping behavior.
Define the payroll handoff and its cutoff, exception, correction, and failure behavior.
Define vendor-neutral corporate-card payment initiation and reconciliation behavior.
Define ordering and rejection behavior for two-manager approval.
Define the consequence of a missing required receipt.
Define currency, precision, rounding, credit, and zero-amount treatment for thresholds.

decisions: Use STANDARD GAL mode because the supplied scope spans approval policy, categorization, receipts, two payment paths, resubmission, and timeliness.
Keep unresolved implementation-affecting choices explicit rather than inventing stakeholder answers.
